sanskrit: samyan digbhyaḥ pavate saṃ svarvin madhor ato mādhavaḥ pātv asmān | agnir devo duṣṭarītur adābhya idaṃ kṣatraṃ rakṣatu pātv asmān ||
english: From all the quarters it blows together, resonant with heaven; from thence may Mādhava protect us with sweetness. May Agni the god, hard to cross, undeceivable, guard this sovereign power and protect us.

sanskrit: rathantaraṃ sāmabhiḥ pātv asmān gāyatreṇa cchandasā viśvarūpam | dvādaśā iṣṭayā stomo ahnāṃ samudro vāca idam ojaḥ pipartu ||
english: May the Rathantara protect us with its sāman-chants, all-formed with the Gāyatrī metre. By the twelve-day sacrifice the praise-hymn of the days — may the ocean of speech fill this might.

sanskrit: ugrā diśām abhibhūtir vayodhāḥ śuciḥ śukre ahany ojasye | indrādhipatiḥ pipṛtād ato no mayi kṣatraṃ viśvato dhārayedam ||
english: Fierce the conquest of the quarters, sustainer of life, pure on the bright day of might. With Indra as overlord, may he fill us from thence; may he uphold in me this sovereign power from all sides.

sanskrit: bṛhad rāṣṭraṃ kṣatrabṛd vṛddhavṛṣṇyaṃ triṣṭubhaujaḥ śubhitam ugravīram | indra stomaiḥ pañcadaśena varca idaṃ vātena sagareṇa rakṣatu ||
english: The great kingship, bearing the warrior-power, with grown virility, adorned with the strength of the Triṣṭubh, of fierce heroism — may Indra guard this lustre with praises through the fifteenfold, together with the wind and the ocean.

sanskrit: prācī diśāṃ sahayaśā yaśasvatī viśve devāḥ prāvṛṣāhnāṃ svarvatī | idaṃ kṣatraṃ duṣṭaram astv ojo anādhṛṣṭaṃ sahasvaṃ sahasvat ||
english: The eastern quarter, sharing in glory, itself glorious; all the gods, the luminous one on the days of the rainy season — let this sovereign power be hard to cross, its might unconquered, overpowering, one that overpowers.

sanskrit: vairūpe sāmany aha tac chakeyaṃ jagatyainad vikṣv ā veśayāmi | viśve devāḥ saptadaśena vadyam idaṃ kṣatraṃ salilāvatam ugram ||
english: In the Vairūpa sāman I declare this — may I be able; with the Jagatī metre I make it enter among the clans. All the gods by the seventeenfold — this fierce sovereign power, accompanied by flood-waters.

sanskrit: dhatrī diśāṃ kṣatram idaṃ dādhartu- -upasthāśānāṃ mitravad astv ojaḥ | mitrāvaruṇā śaradāhnā cikitnū asmai kṣatrāya mahi śarma yacchatam ||
english: May the supporting quarter uphold this sovereign power; among those who hope for refuge may the might be as Mitra. May Mitra and Varuṇa, discerning on the autumnal days, grant great shelter to this sovereign power.

sanskrit: vairāje sāmany adhi me manīṣā- -anuṣṭubhā saṃbhṛtaṃ vīryaṃ sahaḥ | idaṃ kṣatraṃ mitravad ārdradānv ojā mitrāvaruṇā rakṣatam ādhipatye ||
english: In the Vairāja sāman rests my wisdom; the virile force and might gathered through the Anuṣṭubh. May Mitra and Varuṇa protect this sovereign power, Mitra-like, with moist-giving strength, unto overlordship.

sanskrit: samrāḍ diśāṃ sahasāmnī sahasvaty ṛtur hemanto viṣṭhayā naḥ pipartu | oṣajātāṃ bṛhatī ca śakvarī- -imaṃ yajñam avatāṃ no ghṛtācī ||
english: The universal sovereign of the quarters, the powerful one whose sāmans are of might — may the season of winter fill us through its extension. May the Bṛhatī and Śakvarī, born from healing, and the ghee-bright one protect this sacrifice of ours.

sanskrit: svarvatī sudughā naḥ payasvatī diśāṃ devy avatu no ghṛtācī | tvaṃ gopāḥ puraetota paścād bṛhaspate yāmyāṃ yuṅdhi vācam ||
english: The heavenly one of good milking, rich in milk for us — may the divine goddess of the quarters, the ghee-bright one, protect us. You are guardian before and behind; O Bṛhaspati, yoke the southward speech.

sanskrit: stomaikaviṃśe bhuvanasya patni vivasvagvāte abhi no gṛṇīhi | ghṛtavatī savitar ādhipatye payasvatī rantir āśā no astu ||
english: O mistress of existence in the twenty-one-fold praise, in the wind pervading all — sing out for us. May the direction rich in ghee, O Savitṛ, unto overlordship; the direction rich in milk be our delight.

sanskrit: ūrdhvā diśāṃ rantir āśauṣadhīnāṃ saṃvatsareṇa savitā no ahnā | revat sāmnāṃ paṅktiś chandasām ajātaśatruḥ syonā no astu ||
english: The upward quarter, the delight of the directions, of the plants — may Savitṛ impel us through the year, through the day. Rich in the Paṅkti of sāmans and metres — may the one who has no born enemy be comfortable to us.

sanskrit: viṣṭambho divo dharuṇaḥ pṛthivyā asyeśānā jagato viṣṇupatnī | viśvavyacā iṣayantī suhutiḥ syonā no astv aditer upasthe ||
english: The pillar of heaven, the support of the earth, the mistress of this world, wife of Viṣṇu — may she who quickens, all-pervading, of good oblation, be comfortable to us in the lap of Aditi.

sanskrit: dhruvā diśāṃ viṣṇupatny aghorā- -asyeśānā sahaso yā manotā | bṛhaspatir mātariśvota vāyuḥ saṃdhānā vātā abhi no gṛṇantu ||
english: The firm quarter, wife of Viṣṇu, not terrible, mistress of this — she who was thought of through might: may Bṛhaspati, Mātariśvan, and Vāyu, the joining winds, sing out for us.

sanskrit: yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhartā yo naḥ sato abhy ā saj jajāna | sa āśiṣā draviṇam icchamānaḥ prathamacchado vara ā viveśa ||
english: He who is our father, our begetter, our disposer, who engendered among the existent what truly exists — he, desiring wealth through blessing, has entered into the first covering, into the boon.

sanskrit: abhy ā vartasva pṛthivī yajñena payasā saha | apānto agnir iṣito 'va rohatu ||
english: Turn toward us, O Earth, together with the sacrifice, together with milk. May Agni, urged onward, the drinker of the final share, descend.

sanskrit: yad agne candraṃ yat pūtaṃ yac chukraṃ yac ca yajñiyam | tad devebhyo bharāmasi ||
english: Whatever is bright in thee, O Agni, whatever is pure, whatever is radiant, and whatever is fit for sacrifice — that we bring to the gods.

sanskrit: iṣam ūrjam aham ata ādi yajñasya yonau mahiṣasya dhāman | ā no goṣu viśastv ā prajāyāṃ jahāmi sedim anirām amīvām ||
english: Refreshment and vigour — I take these hence from the womb of sacrifice, from the abode of the great one. May it enter into our cattle, into our offspring; I cast away languor, debility, and disease.

sanskrit: āyuṣo 'si prataraṇaṃ vipraṃ bheṣajam ucyase | tad āñjana tvaṃ śantāte 'si māyobhavaṃ kṛtam ||
english: You are the prolonger of life, you are called the inspired medicine. Therefore, O Añjana, you are for our peace — made into that which brings well-being.

sanskrit: yo harimā jāyānyo aṅgabhedo visalpakaḥ | sarvaṃ te yakṣmam aṅgebhyo bahir nir hantv āñjanam ||
english: The jaundice that arises again and again, the splitting of limbs, the visalpaka fever — let the añjana drive out entirely your every disease from your limbs to the outside.

sanskrit: āñjanaṃ pṛthivyāṃ jātaṃ bhadraṃ puruṣajīvanam | kṛṇotv atpramāyakaṃ rathajūtim anāgasam ||
english: The añjana, born from the earth, auspicious, life-giving to man — may it produce what is not ruinous, swift as a chariot, free from sin.

sanskrit: prāṇa prāṇaṃ trāyasvāso asave mṛḍa | nirṛte nirṛtyā naḥ pāśebhyo muñca ||
english: O Prāṇa, protect breath; O breath, be gracious to the living. O Nirṛti, free us from the bonds of dissolution.

sanskrit: sindhor garbho 'si vidyutāṃ puṣpam | vātaḥ prāṇaḥ sūryaś cakṣur divas payaḥ ||
english: You are the womb of the Sindhu, the flower of lightnings. The wind is breath, the sun is sight, the milk of heaven.

sanskrit: devāñjanaṃ traikakudaṃ pari mā pāhi viśvataḥ | na tvā taranty oṣadhayo bāhyāḥ parvatīyā uta ||
english: O divine Añjana, O Traikakuda, protect me on all sides. Neither the external herbs nor the mountain ones surpass you.

sanskrit: vīdaṃ madhyam avāsṛjad rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ | amīvāḥ sarvāś cātayan nāśayad abhibhā itaḥ ||
english: He released the strong middle portion — the destroyer of demons, the disperser of disease. Driving away all diseases, destroying them, the overpowering one expelled them from here.

sanskrit: bahv idaṃ rājan varuṇa- -anṛtam āha puruṣaḥ | tasmāt sahasravīrya muñca naḥ pary aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Much falsehood, O King Varuṇa, has a man spoken. From that, O you of a thousand powers, free us from transgression on every side.

sanskrit: yad āpo aghnyā iti varuṇeti yad ūcima | tasmāt sahasravīrya muñca naḥ pary aṃhasaḥ ||
english: What we have said — \"O inviolable waters,\" \"O Varuṇa\" — from that, O you of a thousand powers, free us from transgression on every side.

sanskrit: mitraś ca tvā varuṇaś ca- -anu preyatur āñjana | tau tvānugatya dūraṃ bhogāya puna rohatu ||
english: May Mitra and Varuṇa follow after you, O Añjana. Having followed you far, may it grow again for enjoyment.
